quests.instruction: Every morning, Sam plays football in the park. Yesterday he also ___ football in the park.
quests.hint: 'Yesterday' tells you that the action is finished.
quests.explanation: Play becomes 'played' when something happened in the past. Most verbs just add -ed.
quests.funFact: Most English verbs add -ed to talk about the past.

quests.instruction: Last Sunday, Ravi ___ all the way to the lake with his grandfather.
quests.hint: 'Last Sunday' means it is already finished.
quests.explanation: Walk becomes 'walked' for something that is over: We walked to the lake.
quests.funFact: The -ed ending sounds different in 'walked', 'played' and 'wanted'.

quests.instruction: Dad asks, 'Did you ___ your homework?' Mia answers, 'Yes, I finished it an hour ago.'
quests.hint: After 'did', the main verb goes back to its simple form.
quests.explanation: After 'did', the main verb stays in its simple form: Did you do it? 'Did' already shows the past.
quests.funFact: 'Did' is one of the most useful little words for making English questions.

quests.instruction: Last night, we ___ rice and chicken for dinner.
quests.hint: 'Last night' means that the meal is over.
quests.explanation: Eat is irregular, so its past is 'ate' and not 'eated'.
quests.funFact: 'Ate' sounds exactly like the number 'eight'.

quests.instruction: Priya's family ___ to the sea last summer.
quests.hint: Think about the past of 'go'.
quests.explanation: Go changes completely in the past: 'went'. It is an irregular verb.
quests.funFact: 'Went' was once the past of a different, older verb, 'wend'.

quests.instruction: 'What did you see at the zoo?' 'I ___ a baby elephant!'
quests.hint: The answer is about a past visit.
quests.explanation: See becomes 'saw' in the past: I saw a baby elephant.
quests.funFact: 'Saw' is also a cutting tool, but the two words are used differently.

quests.instruction: Our visitors ___ at five o'clock yesterday and left at nine.
quests.hint: 'Yesterday' tells you that the visit has finished.
quests.explanation: Come becomes 'came': they came, we came, she came.
quests.funFact: 'Became' is the past of 'become', and it contains 'came'.

quests.instruction: Zoe ___ the bus to school this morning because it was raining.
quests.hint: 'This morning' is already in the past.
quests.explanation: Take becomes 'took' in the past.
quests.funFact: 'Took' rhymes with 'book'.

quests.instruction: Aunt Rina ___ me a lovely book for my birthday last week.
quests.hint: The gift has already been handed over.
quests.explanation: Give becomes 'gave' in the past: She gave me a book.
quests.funFact: 'Gave' is the simple past, and 'given' is used after 'have': I have been given a book.

quests.instruction: Hana ___ a paper boat and put it on the water.
quests.hint: The boat is finished.
quests.explanation: Make becomes 'made' in the past.
quests.funFact: Many products have a label that says 'made in' followed by the name of a country.

quests.instruction: When the bell rang, the children ___ out of the classroom.
quests.hint: The bell has already rung.
quests.explanation: Run becomes 'ran' in the past.
quests.funFact: The verb 'run' has hundreds of different meanings in big dictionaries.

quests.instruction: Kofi ___ a letter to his friend last night and posted it this morning.
quests.hint: The letter is finished.
quests.explanation: Write becomes 'wrote' in the past.
quests.funFact: 'Wrote' sounds like the word 'rote', as in learning something by heart.

quests.instruction: Leo asks, 'Where is my pencil?' Mia answers, 'Sorry, I ___ it from your desk to sharpen it. Here it is.'
quests.hint: She moved it from his desk, and she did not hand it to anyone else.
quests.explanation: Take, in the past 'took', means to get something and move it away. 'Lent' would mean that she let someone else use it.
quests.funFact: The word 'sorry' is one of the first polite words that children learn in English.

quests.instruction: The ice cream stayed in the sun for an hour, so it ___ and dripped onto Dev's hand.
quests.hint: Heat is the cause here.
quests.explanation: Melt, in the past 'melted', describes what happens when heat turns something solid into liquid.
quests.funFact: Ice cream melts quickly because it is made to be soft at a few degrees above freezing.

quests.instruction: First Tara filled the kettle with water, then she ___ it on, and finally she poured the tea.
quests.hint: This is the step that makes the water hot.
quests.explanation: Switch on means to start a machine by using a switch. In the past it is 'switched on'.
quests.funFact: Some kettles switch themselves off when the water boils.

quests.instruction: Kofi tells his teacher, 'My bus ___ down on the way, so I walked the rest.'
quests.hint: It explains why he had to walk.
quests.explanation: Break down means to stop working. A machine, like a bus, can break down.
quests.funFact: 'Break down' can also mean to start crying.

quests.instruction: Sara wrote the answer on the board, but Ben made it disappear with a cloth. Ben ___ it.
quests.hint: The writing was removed.
quests.explanation: Erase means to remove writing. Ben erased the answer, so it was no longer on the board.
quests.funFact: Whiteboards and chalkboards both use a cloth for erasing.

quests.instruction: The lid of the jam jar is stuck. Dad wraps a cloth around it and tries to ___ it open.
quests.hint: The lid is round, and the movement goes around.
quests.explanation: Twist means to turn something by holding it at two ends or around its centre. A lid is twisted open.
quests.funFact: A wet lid is slippery, but a dry cloth gives you a better grip.

quests.instruction: Because Noor ___ her homework carefully, she found two small mistakes before handing it in.
quests.hint: She looked at it again to make sure.
quests.explanation: Check means to look carefully to make sure something is right. 'Checked' is its past form.
quests.funFact: Checking your work is easier if you take a short break first.

quests.instruction: Max skipped breakfast, and by midday he was so hungry that his stomach ___.
quests.hint: It was making a noise that told everyone he was hungry.
quests.explanation: Growl means to make a low, rough sound. A hungry stomach can growl.
quests.funFact: Your stomach makes its noise when food, liquid and air move around inside it.

quests.instruction: The soup was too hot, so Ella ___ on it gently before she took a sip.
quests.hint: She wanted to make it cooler.
quests.explanation: Blow means to push air out through your lips. 'Blew' is its past form.
quests.funFact: Blowing on hot food cools it because the moving air carries heat away.

quests.instruction: When you make an omelette, you first ___ the eggs into a bowl, and then you whisk them.
quests.hint: The shells must be opened before anything else.
quests.explanation: Crack means to break open. Eggs are cracked before they are whisked.
quests.funFact: Cracking an egg on a flat surface keeps small bits of shell from falling in.

quests.instruction: First Hana measured the flour, then she ___ it into the bowl, and finally she stirred the batter.
quests.hint: Between measuring and stirring, the flour has to go into the bowl.
quests.explanation: Pour means to make something flow from one container to another. 'Poured' is its past form.
quests.funFact: Pouring from a small height makes less mess than pouring from a high one.

quests.instruction: Before crossing the road, Ben stopped, looked both ways and ___ until all the cars had passed.
quests.hint: It was the safe thing to do.
quests.explanation: Wait means to stay in one place until something happens. 'Waited' is its past form.
quests.funFact: Many countries teach children to stop, look and listen before they cross.

quests.instruction: The cat did not run at the bird. Instead, it ___ slowly along the wall, keeping its body low.
quests.hint: It moved slowly and quietly.
quests.explanation: Creep means to move slowly and carefully, with the body low. Its past form is 'crept'.
quests.funFact: The word 'crept' is irregular: it does not take -ed.

quests.instruction: Rina did not shout across the library. Instead, she ___ her question to the librarian.
quests.hint: A library needs quiet.
quests.explanation: Whisper means to speak in a very soft voice. It is a good choice in a quiet place.
quests.funFact: Librarians sometimes put up a sign with a finger over the lips to ask for quiet.

quests.instruction: The old man did not rush across the park. He ___ along the path, enjoying the flowers.
quests.hint: He took his time.
quests.explanation: Stroll means to walk in a slow, relaxed way. 'Strolled' is its past form.
quests.funFact: A stroll is a walk you take for pleasure, not to get somewhere fast.

quests.instruction: In the playground, a small child is crying alone near the swings. What is the kindest action?
quests.hint: The child needs somebody's kindness.
quests.explanation: Comfort means to help someone feel better when they are sad or upset.
quests.funFact: Even a few kind words can help a worried child feel safe.

quests.instruction: A classmate drops all her books in the corridor, and they go everywhere. What should you do?
quests.hint: She needs someone to lend a hand.
quests.explanation: Help means to do something useful for someone in trouble.
quests.funFact: Offering help does not take long, but it can mean a lot to someone.

quests.instruction: You break your friend's toy by accident. What is the best thing to do?
quests.hint: It was an accident, but it is still honest to say something.
quests.explanation: Apologise means to say sorry for what you did. An honest apology helps friends stay friends.
quests.funFact: An apology is stronger when it says what happened and offers to put it right.
